children: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (NSE:BPCL) is navigating a squeeze: RBI opened a special dollar window to meet its FX needs and curb spot demand while BPCL has held retail diesel prices since May—absorbing ~Rs20/l loss—boosting sales ~25.4% YoY even as it alters ethanol and tender sourcing.
RBI Special Dollar Window For BPCL

: RBI opened a special dollar window from Oct 12 to supply BPCL’s daily foreign currency needs via designated banks, routing purchases through forex reserves, cutting BPCL’s spot-market dollar demand.
BPCL Keeps Retail Diesel Prices Steady
: Bharat Petroleum (BPCL) kept retail diesel prices unchanged since May, absorbing about Rs 20/litre loss on diesel sales while rivals raised prices and shifted supplies to exports.
BPCL Tender Details And Ethanol Incentives
: BPCL bid in a tender excluding sugarcane juice/syrup and B-heavy molasses. Maize ethanol incentive cut to Rs2.79/l and corn-based procurement price lowered to Rs68.86/l.
: BPCL diesel sales rose ~25.4% YoY to 3.65 million tonnes in early October, boosted by festival transport, stronger farm demand and lower public pump prices versus private outlets.
